24ea87a563da: Salesforce Campaign Dates: Every Event Day, No Apex
d3816db9666e: Track every date of a Salesforce Campaign on one calendar: tour stops, webinar series and volunteer days saved as child records, with status colors. No Apex.
926527f7845b: Can a Salesforce Campaign have multiple dates?
3692b287e454: A standard Campaign has one Start Date and one End Date. To track every day of a tour, webinar series or volunteer program, add a small child object with a lookup to Campaign and put the MultiDatePick Dates component on the Campaign record page. Every date you click is saved as its own child record.
3f5d3dbdcd13: Do I need Apex or a developer to add dates to Campaigns?
652325b30011: No. The child object and its fields are point-and-click in Object Manager, the Setup Wizard writes the calendar configuration, and the component goes on the page in Lightning App Builder. There is no Campaign-specific code to write or install.
6ed625117e5e: Where are the Campaign dates stored?
119342a8406f: In your own custom object, for example Campaign Date, with one record per date and a lookup to the Campaign. They are ordinary Salesforce records, so list views, reports, flows and sharing all work on them as usual.
0fd0196277e0: Can each Campaign date have its own status?
6520599ffd46: Yes. Add a picklist such as Planned, Confirmed, Completed and Cancelled, choose a color for each value, and the calendar paints every date in its status color. Edit mode lets you select several dates and change their status, move them, or delete them in one step.
11477a0fafa3: Can I use it in a Screen Flow instead of the record page?
e0cc3f90d19a: Yes. Add the Dates component to a flow screen and set Config Name to the config you saved in the Setup Wizard. Pass the Campaign Id into Parent Record Id and the component saves the child records itself, or leave it blank and loop the Selected Dates output.

8c1af7212aee: A Campaign has one start date and one end date. Your tour, webinar series or volunteer program has many. Put them all on the Campaign record, each one a real record with a status, without writing Apex.
a606dc7794a9: "How do I add more than one date to a Salesforce Campaign?" "Where do I track each stop of the roadshow?" "Which webinar sessions are confirmed?" A Campaign only knows when it starts and ends. Everything in between ends up in a spreadsheet or a long description field.

7c96c85bff73: Set it up in three steps
7fd200b671d2: The components are object-agnostic. They do not know or care that the parent is a Campaign; they need a child object to save into and a lookup that points back. That is the whole integration.
4968f1cd173c: <t1>Create the child object.</t1> In Object Manager, create a custom object such as <t2>Campaign Date</t2>. Give it a Lookup field to Campaign and a Date field. Add a Status picklist (Planned, Confirmed, Completed, Cancelled) and any detail fields you want on hover, such as Venue.
540f50522493: <t1>Run the Setup Wizard.</t1> Open the MultiDatePick Setup Wizard tab and configure the Dates component. Pick Campaign Date as the object, the Campaign lookup as the relationship field and your Date field. On Status & Display, choose the status field, a color per value and the hover fields. Save the config under a name like <t2>Campaign_Dates</t2>.
999b3c0f4d37: <t1>Drop the component on the Campaign page.</t1> Open any Campaign, click Edit Page, drag the MultiDatePick Dates component onto the layout and enter the config name in <t2>Config Name</t2>. Save and activate. Every Campaign now has its calendar.
328e27d661f7: Need times as well as days, like a webinar at 11:00 and a repeat at 3:00? Use the Date Time component instead and add Start and End Time fields to the child object. The steps are the same.
fd1f9361255b: The same config works inside Flow. Add the Dates component to a screen and set <t1>Config Name</t1>; every setting comes from the config, with no checkboxes to set in Flow Builder. Pass the Campaign Id into <t2>Parent Record Id</t2> and the component saves the child records itself. Leave it blank if you would rather loop the Selected Dates output and create the records your own way. The <t3>multiple dates in a Screen Flow</t3> post walks through both patterns.
004a7d574a11: Anything a Campaign does on more than one day fits the same child object:

e9dfe5f64187: <t1>Webinar series</t1><t2>A recurring pattern lays out the whole series; the colors show which sessions have run.</t2>
d5c5a2e25441: <t1>Volunteer days</t1><t2>Service days and drives across a season, each one a record you can report on.</t2>
